subject: Agriculture
title: The Open Field System
description: A 60-second lesson on The Open Field System.

hook.text: Medieval European villages shared their farmland. No fences—just long strips in open fields.

buildup.text: Each family farmed several strips scattered across two or three large fields around the village.

discovery.text: Scattering strips gave everyone a mix of good and poor soil. It was a system of built-in fairness.

twist.text: But nobody could experiment. If your neighbor plowed late, weeds spread to your strip too.

climax.text: The system lasted 800 years across Europe. It fed millions but resisted every attempt at improvement.

punchline.text: Fair but frozen—medieval farming chose equality over innovation.

quiz.question: Why were strips scattered across different fields in the open field system?
options: To give each family a fair mix of soil quality
